title: The strongest restoring turn
hook: Change amplitude and predict maximum acceleration magnitude.
misconception: maximum acceleration magnitude stays fixed when amplitude doubles.
objective: Apply a_max = ω²A to compare maximum acceleration magnitude when amplitude changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With simple harmonic motion with fixed angular frequency, a_max = ω²A. When amplitude doubles, maximum acceleration magnitude becomes 2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model a_max = ω²A; scaling exponent 1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider simple harmonic motion with fixed angular frequency, with a nonzero initial result. If amplitude triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on maximum acceleration magnitude?
recall.why: Apply a_max = ω²A under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 3.
